repositories.brief_summary: Stdlib gained `Option.try_value`/`Result.try_value` and `Obj.hash_variant`, while a new Hashtbl redesign proposal sparked debate.
repositories.new_features_summary: New `Option.try_value`, `Result.try_value`, and `Obj.hash_variant` merged; toplevel gains module-dependent function tracing.
repositories.new_features:
- Standard library gains `Option.try_value` and `Result.try_value`, returning a fallback value or an error handler's result respectively, implemented by [Michael Neumann](https://github.com/mneumann) with review by [Daniel Bünzli](https://github.com/dbuenzli) and [David Allsopp](https://github.com/dra27) ([#14941](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14941))
- `Btype.hash_variant` (the compiler's implementation of the runtime's `caml_hash_variant`) moved to a new public `Obj.hash_variant` function by [David Allsopp](https://github.com/dra27) ([#14939](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14939))
- Toplevel gains limited support for tracing module-dependent functions via `modular explicits`, implemented by [Florian Angeletti](https://github.com/Octachron) ([#14707](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14707))
- Fixed a memory leak in the runtime by bounding the size of the internal fiber/stack cache, work by [Vesa Karvonen](https://github.com/polytypic) and [Florian Angeletti](https://github.com/Octachron), merged by [Florian Angeletti](https://github.com/Octachron) ([#14940](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14940))
- Fixed RISC-V assembler errors from `Ireturn_addr` and `Iextcall` with stack arguments when the offset exceeds a 12-bit immediate, by [Tim McGilchrist](https://github.com/tmcgilchrist) ([#14943](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14943))
- Typing recovery mechanism extended to keep continuation information inside the `Typedtree` via a dedicated type, helping editors report more than one typing error, by [Xavier Van de Woestyne](https://github.com/xvw) ([#14946](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14946), [#14945](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14945))
- Added a level to abbreviations in `Texpand` as part of the ongoing expansion/well-foundedness rework, by [Jacques Garrigue](https://github.com/garrigue) ([#14801](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14801))
- Overhauled the locale-handling code used for mingw/msvc float-to-string and string-to-float conversions in `runtime/floats.c`, by [David Allsopp](https://github.com/dra27) ([#10258](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/10258))
- `OCAMLTOP_INCLUDE_PATH` is now ignored during the build, fixing opam installation failures when the variable holds an invalid value, by [David Allsopp](https://github.com/dra27) ([#14914](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14914))
- Added documentation for the ocamllex `-w` warning-list argument to the man page, covering the `missing-case` warning, by [Jeannalyse](https://github.com/Jeannalyse) ([#14944](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14944), closing [#14902](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14902))
- Updated documentation for runtime functions using `nanosleep`, by [David Allsopp](https://github.com/dra27) ([#14948](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14948))
repositories.activity_summary: New PRs opened spanning a Hashtbl redesign and ctype refactors, while unsafe Dynarray and extensible IO-channel PRs were closed.
repositories.activity:
- [Jeannalyse](https://github.com/Jeannalyse) opened a draft **reimplementation of Hashtbl** giving deterministic iteration order regardless of the random seed, as a final contribution from a research internship with [Gabriel Scherer](https://github.com/gasche) ([#14956](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14956)); [Florian Angeletti](https://github.com/Octachron) pushed back on trading generic-structure performance for this safety property
- [Gabriel Scherer](https://github.com/gasche) opened a series of **typechecker path-equivalence refactors** in `ctype.ml`, including normalizing types in `tconstr`-equivalence fast paths ([#14950](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14950)), clarifying uses of `Env_unscoped.path_equiv` ([#14947](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14947)), and an optimization for path-equivalence checks modulo normalization built on top of those ([#14952](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14952)), following on from [Florian Angeletti](https://github.com/Octachron)'s path-equivalence-modulo-aliases work ([#14927](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14927))
- [David Allsopp](https://github.com/dra27) opened a PR to bump the required autoconf version to 2.72 ([#14953](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14953)), addressing an issue about CI/local autoconf version mismatches ([#14937](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14937))
- [Khalid](https://github.com/khalidbelk) opened a PR adding `Sys.file_exists'`, a variant raising `Sys_error` on failure instead of returning `false` ([#14951](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14951)), addressing a long-standing request ([#12393](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/12393))
- [Benoit](https://github.com/benjub) opened a PR adding `Stdlib.Char.Ascii.is_punct`, completing the set of ASCII predicates left out of an earlier PR ([#14957](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14957))
- [Stefan Muenzel](https://github.com/smuenzel) opened PRs for smaller generated code for stack reallocation on AMD64 ([#14954](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14954)) and a fix for expect-test trailing output ([#14959](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14959)), alongside earlier open work inlining the full-application part of `caml_apply` ([#14925](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14925)) and eliding the occurs-check for fresh-variable parameters ([#14913](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14913))
- [Gabriel Scherer](https://github.com/gasche) opened a PR disabling `testsuite/tests/misc/sorts.ml`, noting it is a benchmark rather than a correctness test ([#14960](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14960)), and briefly opened then closed a `ocamlc -g` reoptimization attempt ([#14961](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14961))
- [Simon Cruanes](https://github.com/c-cube) closed his **extensible IO channels** RFC implementation, noting stdlib-committee discussion had stalled ([#14775](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14775)), and closed `Buffer.iter_chunks` ([#12931](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/12931))
- [Gabriel Scherer](https://github.com/gasche) closed `Dynarray.unsafe_{get,set}` after concluding the safety-reasoning tradeoffs were not worth the 1.4-2.5x microbenchmark speedup, following questions from [Daniel Bünzli](https://github.com/dbuenzli) ([#14864](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14864))
- [v-gb](https://github.com/v-gb) closed a PR improving `Map`/`Set.union` complexity on related maps after [Gabriel Scherer](https://github.com/gasche) identified it violated the `union` specification when the merge function is non-trivial; [Nicolás Ojeda Bär](https://github.com/nojb) noted the `Set.union` fast path remained valid and that LexiFi has related `inter`/`diff` optimizations to offer ([#14949](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14949))
- Ongoing open work continues on structured compiler diagnostics for developer tooling by [Florian Angeletti](https://github.com/Octachron) ([#13766](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/13766)), new GC-pacing logic by [Damien Doligez](https://github.com/damiendoligez) ([#14796](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14796)), link-time linking support by [Raphaël Proust](https://github.com/raphael-proust) ([#14895](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14895)), exposing `caml_ba_compare` and related bigarray functions by [David Allsopp](https://github.com/dra27) ([#14804](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14804)), and POWER-architecture frame-pointer support by [Tim McGilchrist](https://github.com/tmcgilchrist) ([#14505](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14505))
- Cross-platform build maintenance continued with [David Allsopp](https://github.com/dra27)'s build-environment sanitization ([#14915](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14915)) and macOS opam-sandbox compiler-cloning fix ([#14923](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14923)), [Antonin Décimo](https://github.com/MisterDA)'s Cygwin build fixes ([#14921](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14921)) and `CAMLthread_local` C/C++ interoperability improvement ([#14934](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14934)), and [Kate](https://github.com/kit-ty-kate)'s macOS fix for `opam clone` ([#14901](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14901))
- Runtime fixes remain open for a musl/Intel `sigaltstack` issue by [Nat Mote](https://github.com/nmote) ([#14933](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14933)), printing `errno` on `sigaltstack` errors by [Nathan Taylor](https://github.com/dijkstracula) ([#14928](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14928)), and dropping redundant memory-model fences around atomic RMWs on AArch64 by [Sebastian Pop](https://github.com/sebpop) ([#14936](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14936))
- [Gabriel Scherer](https://github.com/gasche) has an open fix for record updates with unchanged `[@atomic]` fields ([#14935](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14935)), addressing a reported issue where functional updates of atomic records fail to emit atomic loads ([#14918](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14918))
repositories.discussions_summary: A proposed Hashtbl rewrite for deterministic iteration order and a String search-function discussion drew debate.
repositories.notable_discussions:
- [Jeannalyse](https://github.com/Jeannalyse)'s draft Hashtbl reimplementation for deterministic iteration order drew disagreement from [Florian Angeletti](https://github.com/Octachron), who argued against slowing down a performance-sensitive generic data structure to guard against programmer error ([#14956](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14956))
- [Daniel Bünzli](https://github.com/dbuenzli) opened a "Show and tell" discussion proposing new `String` search functions (`find_sub`/`rfind_sub`) based on a two-way string-search algorithm, following up on [#14068](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14068), with a gist and benchmark script for feedback ([#14099](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/discussions/14099))
- [Austin Theriault](https://github.com/ajbt200128) described Semgrep's need for per-domain timeouts and discussed with [Gabriel Scherer](https://github.com/gasche) whether `Domain.interrupt` can safely interact with effect handlers, referencing the asynchronous-exception-masking work in [#8961](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/8961) ([#14955](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14955))
- The autoconf version mismatch between CI and local hygiene checks was debated by [Antonin Décimo](https://github.com/MisterDA), [David Allsopp](https://github.com/dra27), and others, weighing bleeding-edge autoconf against long-term stability ([#14937](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14937))
- [Simon Cruanes](https://github.com/c-cube)'s extensible IO channels RFC implementation was closed after stdlib-committee discussion stalled without a resolution ([#14775](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14775))
repositories.trends_summary: Continued stdlib performance-vs-safety tradeoffs and a cluster of cross-platform build and locale fixes.
repositories.emerging_trends:

repositories.brief_summary: opam 2.6.0-alpha1 was released and published, followed by quick triage of a release-signature mixup and a git fsmonitor bug.
repositories.new_features_summary: Install scripts updated for the opam 2.6.0-alpha1 release, which bundles root/rootexec install sections and --ignore-available-on.
repositories.new_features:
- Install scripts (`shell/install.sh`, `shell/install.ps1`) were updated to fetch and verify **opam 2.6.0-alpha1** binaries, adding SHA512 checksums for arm64/armhf/i686/ppc64le/riscv64/s390x-linux and x86_64-freebsd/macos/netbsd/openbsd/windows builds ([#7047](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/pull/7047), [3fb3330](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/commit/3fb333011162fc6c722708e2c1c28126219c700d))
- The **opam 2.6.0-alpha1** release published this week by [Kate](https://github.com/kit-ty-kate) bundles the `root` and `rootexec` `.install` file sections for installing files relative to the prefix root ([#6938](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/6938)), a new `--ignore-available-on` flag to bypass a package's `available:` constraints ([#6836](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/6836)), and a performance fix that skips default-compiler selection during `opam init --bare` ([#6957](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/6957))
- Source-compatibility changes for newer **cmdliner** versions were folded into the release, paving the way for the in-progress cmdliner-based completion rewrite ([#6854](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/6854))
- A draft fix is in progress for **line-wrapped `opam env` output**, where the shell command to update the environment was breaking across lines and could not be copy-pasted ([#7051](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/pull/7051), fixes [#7050](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/7050))
repositories.activity_summary: Kate merged the alpha1 install-script PR and opened three follow-ups; WardBrian's cmdliner completion series and yannl35133's error-message PR remain open.
repositories.activity:
- Three **new PRs opened** this week remain unmerged: a version bump to `2.6.0~alpha2~dev` preparing the next development cycle by [Kate](https://github.com/kit-ty-kate) ([#7048](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/pull/7048)), a draft fix for line-wrapped `opam env` output ([#7051](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/pull/7051)), and a draft upgrade of the generated autoconf files to 2.72 ([#7052](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/pull/7052))
- [Kate](https://github.com/kit-ty-kate) merged the install-script preparation for the **2.6.0-alpha1** release ([#7047](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/pull/7047)) and published the release itself the same day
- [Brian Ward](https://github.com/WardBrian) continues the multi-PR **cmdliner-based completion overhaul**: environment variables for bash/zsh completion ([#6812](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/pull/6812)), the cmdliner vendor update to 2.1.1 ([#6867](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/pull/6867)), argument definitions wired up with completion functions ([#6868](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/pull/6868)), and installing the new cmdliner-based completion scripts with PowerShell support ([#6869](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/pull/6869))
- [yannl35133](https://github.com/yannl35133) opened a PR making the `opam repo add` error message more explicit, fixing [#6943](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/6943) ([#7014](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/pull/7014))
repositories.discussions_summary: A release-signature key mixup and a git fsmonitor socket bug were reported and diagnosed within a day of the 2.6.0-alpha1 release.
repositories.notable_discussions:
- The **2.6.0-alpha1 release signature** was found to use the wrong GPG subkey shortly after publishing; [Andriy Sultanov](https://github.com/last-genius) reported the verification failure and [Kate](https://github.com/kit-ty-kate) traced it to a `--export-secret-subkeys` key-transfer mistake, removed the errant subkey, and re-signed the release artifacts the same day ([#7049](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/7049))

repositories.brief_summary: Rudi Grinberg landed LSP trace notifications, a Dune-file code action, and dozens of protocol fixes alongside a large OCaml test-suite rewrite.
repositories.new_features_summary: New Dune trace notifications, an open-Dune-file code action, operator semantic highlighting, plus completion/code-action/URI protocol fixes.
repositories.new_features:
- Dune RPC calls, build-progress updates, and Merlin configuration activity are now reported through LSP **trace notifications**, giving clients visibility into background server work ([#1899](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/1899)) by [Rudi Grinberg](https://github.com/rgrinberg).
- Added a **code action to open the closest Dune file** for the current document ([#1817](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/1817), fixes [#1491](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/1491)) by [Rudi Grinberg](https://github.com/rgrinberg).
- **Semantic highlighting** now distinguishes operators from ordinary functions ([#1831](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/1831)) by [Rudi Grinberg](https://github.com/rgrinberg).
- **Semantic-token capability negotiation** was tightened so support is only advertised to clients that declare the capability, support the relative token format, support full-document requests, or request delta support, respectively ([#1851](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/1851), [#1853](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/1853), [#1856](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/1856), [#1859](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/1859)) by [Rudi Grinberg](https://github.com/rgrinberg).
- **Completion** correctness fixes landed for a lone polymorphic-variant backtick (fixes [#1427](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/1427)), the client's preferred documentation format, non-ASCII prefixes and CRLF whitespace, constructor kinds for clients without enum-member support, deprecation tags, and lexical sort-key ordering beyond 9,999 items ([#1823](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/1823), [#1885](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/1885), [#1886](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/1886), [#1887](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/1887), [#1903](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/1903), [#1883](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/1883)) by [Rudi Grinberg](https://github.com/rgrinberg).
- **Code actions** now advertise all kinds the server may return and compute correct ranges after multiline text insertions ([#1803](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/1803), [#1748](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/1748)) by [Rudi Grinberg](https://github.com/rgrinberg).
- Fixed `textDocument/documentSymbol` to return a `selectionRange` contained within its `range`, so clients no longer reject the document outline (fixes [#1560](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/1560)) ([#1775](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/1775)) by [Leonardo Scappatura](https://github.com/Leonard013).
- **URI parsing and serialization** correctness fixes covered query parameters bleeding into filesystem paths, paths beginning with two slashes, percent-encoded fragments, non-letter Windows-drive-like segments, and unescaped Unicode in query components ([#1776](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/1776), [#1798](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/1798), [#1801](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/1801), [#1800](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/1800), [#1799](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/1799)) by [Rudi Grinberg](https://github.com/rgrinberg).
- Document **offsets are now preserved across incremental text edits** ([#1777](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/1777)) by [Rudi Grinberg](https://github.com/rgrinberg).
- Fixed handling of **zero-work Dune build progress** updates ([#1896](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/1896)) by [Rudi Grinberg](https://github.com/rgrinberg).
- Stopped **workspace-symbol searches** from warning when a workspace has not yet been built ([#1769](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/1769)) by [Sora Morimoto](https://github.com/smorimoto).
- **JSON-RPC** hardening: negative `Content-Length` headers are now rejected, and unsupported LSP request methods are reported as unavailable instead of raising an internal server error ([#1873](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/1873), [#1862](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/1862)) by [Rudi Grinberg](https://github.com/rgrinberg).
repositories.activity_summary: Twenty PRs opened this week refine LSP diagnostics, completion, and code actions, while a large OCaml test-suite rewrite closes a long-standing issue.
repositories.activity:
- Work on **LSP diagnostic and code-action protocol** features remains open, including `textDocument/diagnostic` pulls that query Dune RPC for its latest diagnostic snapshot ([#1782](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/1782)), code-action kind filtering that follows the hierarchical `.`-separated kind spec ([#1802](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/1802)), and lazy code-action edit resolution via `codeAction/resolve` ([#1808](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/1808)), all opened by [Rudi Grinberg](https://github.com/rgrinberg).

- **Server lifecycle and JSON-RPC** hardening was merged, including deterministic shutdown ([#1745](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/1745)), halting Dune/Merlin readers on shutdown ([#1770](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/1770)), deferring dynamic registration until initialization completes ([#1876](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/1876)), rejecting ambiguous JSON-RPC response objects ([#1870](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/1870)), and hardening the pending-request lifecycle ([#1875](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/1875)).

repositories.new_features_summary: New destruct support for open record patterns, an exposed warnings-parsing API, and fixes for locate/occurrences staleness.
repositories.new_features:
- Destruct now closes **open record patterns** into fully closed ones (turning `{ b = _; _ }` into `{ b = _; a; c }`) by [Paul-Elliot Anglès d'Auriac](https://github.com/panglesd), resolving a feature request open since 2015 ([#2103](https://github.com/ocaml/merlin/issues/2103), fixes [#436](https://github.com/ocaml/merlin/issues/436))
- Fixed **occurrences staleness detection** never reporting files modified since the index was built, caused by a tuple-evaluation-order bug where the out-of-sync cache was read before it was populated, by [Kostia Balytskyi](https://github.com/ikostia) ([#2104](https://github.com/ocaml/merlin/issues/2104))
- Fixed **`locate` and `document`** resolving `open` paths incorrectly in `.mli` files when a self-shadowing submodule hides the opened module, by making `Open_description` carry the pre-open environment (`browse_raw.mli`), by [Carine Morel](https://github.com/lyrm) ([#2089](https://github.com/ocaml/merlin/issues/2089), fixes [#1748](https://github.com/ocaml/merlin/issues/1748))
- Fixed **occurrences staleness detection** reporting incorrectly when Merlin runs from outside the project's source root, by [Ulysse](https://github.com/voodoos) ([#2097](https://github.com/ocaml/merlin/issues/2097))
- Exposed a `parse_warnings` **API function** (plus new `token`/`modifier` types) in `warnings.mli`, a prerequisite for improved warning-flag handling in ocaml-lsp, by [PixieDust](https://github.com/PizieDust) ([#2088](https://github.com/ocaml/merlin/issues/2088), prerequisite for [ocaml/ocaml-lsp#1606](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/1606) addressing [ocaml/ocaml-lsp#717](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/717))

repositories.discussions_summary: Contributors debated an OCaml 5.5.0 build failure, an LSP outline selection-range bug, and AI-assisted development disclosures.
repositories.notable_discussions:
- [Akhil](https://github.com/akhiltulluri) reported merlin-lib failing to build against **OCaml 5.5.0** with an `Unbound value Seq.delay` error; [Ulysse](https://github.com/voodoos) and [Kate](https://github.com/kit-ty-kate) discussed whether a stale or system-installed stdlib was the cause, without being able to reproduce it on macOS ([#2108](https://github.com/ocaml/merlin/issues/2108))
- [Paul-Elliot Anglès d'Auriac](https://github.com/panglesd) reported the LSP `outline` command emitting a `selection` field with a `None` location outside the entry's own `location`, referencing [ocaml/ocaml-lsp#1773](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/1773) and [ocaml/ocaml-lsp#1775](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/1775) which require selections to stay within their location ([#2106](https://github.com/ocaml/merlin/issues/2106))
- Reviewers on [#2103](https://github.com/ocaml/merlin/issues/2103) debated whether destructured record fields should render as polymorphic or plain variants, and whether `ocamlformat`/`PprintAst` should own that formatting choice
- [Carine Morel](https://github.com/lyrm) disclosed using Claude to help diagnose the `.mli` open-path bug before authoring and reviewing the fix by hand, and clarified with [Paul-Elliot Anglès d'Auriac](https://github.com/panglesd) why `include` (unlike `open`) is unaffected ([#2089](https://github.com/ocaml/merlin/issues/2089))
- [Kostia Balytskyi](https://github.com/ikostia) weighed skipping string-literal contents for hover/documentation purposes against supporting PPX-style `%{name}` interpolation, opting to special-case interpolated segments ([#2098](https://github.com/ocaml/merlin/issues/2098))

repositories.brief_summary: Dune 3.24.1 shipped with a documented opam-CI triage, alongside fish-shell completion, promote-file completion, and an artifact-substitution I/O offload.
repositories.new_features_summary: Fish-shell completion, `dune promote` file completion, background-threaded artifact substitution, and the 3.24.1 patch release shipped this week.
repositories.new_features:
- **Fish shell completion** was added for `dune completion`, covering command, subcommand, and flag completion in the `fish` shell, by [Chizy](https://github.com/chizy7), closing a request from [Ali Caglayan](https://github.com/Alizter) ([#15515](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15515), [#15334](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15334))
- Tab completion for **`dune promote`** now lists pending promotion files instead of only the command's flags, by [Ali Caglayan](https://github.com/Alizter) ([#15338](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15338), fixes [#7254](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/7254))
- Generic **artifact-substitution I/O** (reading/writing substituted files) is now offloaded to the background thread pool instead of running on the scheduler thread, avoiding stalls during large substitutions, by [Antonio Nuno Monteiro](https://github.com/anmonteiro) ([#15559](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15559), [#15598](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15598))
- Fixed a **`sendfile`/`copy_file_range`** bug where a zero-byte transfer at premature EOF left the copy loop retrying forever instead of raising a Unix error, by [Rudi Grinberg](https://github.com/rgrinberg) ([#15554](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15554))
- Fixed `build_runtime_flags` set on a `js_of_ocaml`/`wasm_of_ocaml` executable being silently ignored in separate compilation mode, where such executables incorrectly received the workspace-shared standalone runtime built with default flags, by [Hugo Heuzard](https://github.com/hhugo) ([#15455](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15455))
- Fixed local package binaries in `%{bin:...}` PATH layouts on Windows to use the installed filename rather than the source name, by [Ali Caglayan](https://github.com/Alizter) ([#15518](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15518), fixes [#15512](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15512))
- **Dune 3.24.1** was released, bundling this batch of fixes plus earlier-prepared backports: the `js_of_ocaml` archive-rule internal error for libraries distinguished only by `enabled_if` (credited to [Jérôme Vouillon](https://github.com/vouillon)), formatter actions now receive environment variables correctly, Melange sources get their missing sandbox source dependency, OCaml 5.5+ compiler packages are treated as relocatable, and sandboxing of Melange rules by default was reverted due to per-module sandbox overhead, by [Ali Caglayan](https://github.com/Alizter) and [Shon Feder](https://github.com/shonfeder) ([#15539](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15539))
- Added a CI script (`lint-change-fragments.sh`) that lints `doc/changes/{added,changed,fixed}` changelog fragments, part of the push toward enforcing changelog entries on every user-facing PR
repositories.activity_summary: New PRs target anonymous-action aliasing, `dune describe` output, and a `dune shell` debugger, while a `dune exec` hang was reported and fixed same-day.
repositories.activity:
- Several **PRs opened this week remain unmerged**: reworking anonymous-action registration so a single action can be attached to multiple aliases without surprising inter-alias dependencies, by [Nat Karmios](https://github.com/NatKarmios) ([#15581](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15581), fixes [#15576](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15576)); an `--include-empty` flag for `dune describe external-lib-deps` so libraries with no dependencies are no longer filtered out, by [Nat Karmios](https://github.com/NatKarmios) ([#15585](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15585), fixes [#15566](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15566)); inclusion of anonymous actions in `dune rules` output, following on from [#15581](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15581) ([#15586](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15586)); consistent public/private name handling (with a new `--split-public-names` flag) for `dune describe workspace` and `external-lib-deps`, by [Nat Karmios](https://github.com/NatKarmios) ([#15582](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15582)); a `dune shell` prototype for interactively replaying and editing a rule's action for debugging, by [Ali Caglayan](https://github.com/Alizter) ([#15597](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15597)); and RPC-backed querying of `dune pkg enabled` status so it observes transient server-side settings without acquiring the build lock, by [Ali Caglayan](https://github.com/Alizter), addressing a request from [Tim ats](https://github.com/Tim-ats-d) ([#15589](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15589), fixes [#15587](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15587), with supporting test coverage already merged in [#15588](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15588))

repositories.discussions_summary: 3.24.1's opam-CI triage and the semantics of anonymous actions shared across multiple aliases were the week's main discussion threads.
repositories.notable_discussions:
- [Rudi Grinberg](https://github.com/rgrinberg) and [Nat Karmios](https://github.com/NatKarmios) discussed why anonymous actions attached to multiple aliases produce surprising inter-alias dependencies; Rudi noted `--force` wasn't a strong motivator on its own but agreed human-readable IDs for anonymous actions (useful for `dune shell`) were worth having, prompting a demonstration without `--force` ([#15576](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15576))
- On the **3.24.1 release tracker**, [Ali Caglayan](https://github.com/Alizter) posted a detailed opam-CI triage summary: all 18 release packages checked across 1,314 compiler/distribution/architecture variants with no Dune-attributable regressions, clearing the release for opam publication ([#15439](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15439))
- Also on that tracker, a contributor asked whether a DragonFlyBSD support fix ([#14774](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/14774)) could still be squeezed into 3.24.1; [Ali Caglayan](https://github.com/Alizter) explained that new-platform support isn't appropriate for a patch release reserved for regression fixes, and would instead land in the upcoming 3.25 ([#15439](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15439))
repositories.trends_summary: Describe/rules introspection tooling, dune-pkg/RPC robustness, and a disciplined release process stood out this week.
repositories.emerging_trends:
- **`dune describe`/`dune rules` introspection** is being extended on several fronts at once by [Nat Karmios](https://github.com/NatKarmios): module origin metadata ([#15478](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15478)), an `--include-empty` flag ([#15585](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15585)), anonymous-action visibility ([#15586](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15586)), and public/private name handling ([#15582](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15582)), alongside a new `dune shell` prototype for debugging rule actions from [Ali Caglayan](https://github.com/Alizter) ([#15597](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15597)) — a cluster of developer-experience tooling work
- Continued investment in **`dune pkg` / RPC robustness**: RPC-backed enabled-status checks ([#15589](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15589), [#15588](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15588)) and new failing-test coverage for a concurrent-install race ([#15600](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15600), [#15604](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15604)) ahead of the still-open concurrent install-entries feature ([#13054](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/13054))
- The **3.24.1 patch release** shipped with a documented, metrics-driven opam-reverse-dependency CI triage process before publication ([#15439](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15439)), and the 3.25.0 tracker opened the same week ([#15593](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15593)), pointing to a tightening release cadence
- Incremental **platform-specific correctness fixes** kept landing: Windows bin-layout filenames ([#15518](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15518)), a `sendfile` premature-EOF hang ([#15554](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15554)), and `js_of_ocaml`/`wasm_of_ocaml` runtime-flags handling ([#15455](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15455))

repositories.brief_summary: Detailed commit-by-commit review continued on David Allsopp's open relocatable-ocamlfind PR, with no merges or new commits this week.
repositories.activity_summary: Review of the open relocatable ocamlfind PR continued with detailed feedback from @shym, though nothing merged or was newly opened this week.
repositories.activity:
- [#122](https://github.com/ocaml/ocamlfind/issues/122) ("Relocatable ocamlfind with sprinkles") by [David Allsopp](https://github.com/dra27), which adapts **ocamlfind for OCaml 5.5** and adds support for **relocatable installations** so the same compiler configuration can be installed byte-for-byte identically to different prefixes, received an extensive commit-by-commit review from [@shym](https://github.com/shym) covering `configure` shell-script path handling, the `findlib_config_%.mlp` build rules, and the CI jobs added to verify identical installs on Windows, macOS and Linux ([#122](https://github.com/ocaml/ocamlfind/issues/122)).
- The PR remains open and unmerged; it builds on the `topfind`-generation split from ([#72](https://github.com/ocaml/ocamlfind/issues/72)), fixes relative-path handling for `ld.conf` needed by OCaml 5.5+ ([#115](https://github.com/ocaml/ocamlfind/issues/115)), and addresses non-normalised path comparisons raised in ([#119](https://github.com/ocaml/ocamlfind/issues/119)).
repositories.discussions_summary: Review comments on the relocatable-install PR debated whether relocatability should become Findlib's default posture and how to keep the configure script portable.
repositories.notable_discussions:
- [@shym](https://github.com/shym) suggested that the **relocatable installation** variant should become the default behaviour for Findlib rather than an opt-in mode, in review of [#122](https://github.com/ocaml/ocamlfind/issues/122).
- Reviewers discussed portability trade-offs in the `configure` script, including whether GNU-specific `make`/`sed` incantations are acceptable or whether a POSIX-portable path-trimming helper (proposed as `trim_dotslash`) should be used instead ([#122](https://github.com/ocaml/ocamlfind/issues/122)).
- Naming and readability of the build-variant selection mechanism was debated, including renaming `IS_RELOCATABLE` to `REL_OR_ABS` and using OCaml-style `(*r*)`/`(*a*)` comment markers instead of the existing `x`-prefix convention in `.mlp` template files ([#122](https://github.com/ocaml/ocamlfind/issues/122)).
repositories.trends_summary: Ongoing work is oriented toward relocatable, reproducible Findlib installations ahead of OCaml 5.5.
repositories.emerging_trends: - The in-progress work on [#122](https://github.com/ocaml/ocamlfind/issues/122) reflects a push toward **relocatable, reproducible installations**, following the definition proposed in [ocaml/RFCs#53](https://github.com/ocaml/RFCs/issues/53), ahead of the OCaml 5.5 release.
repositories.contributors_summary: David Allsopp authored the open relocatable-ocamlfind PR while @shym provided extensive commit-by-commit review feedback on it.
repositories.contributors:
- [David Allsopp](https://github.com/dra27) authored the in-progress **relocatable ocamlfind** PR, restructuring `configure`, extending `findlib.conf` relative-path resolution, and adding CI jobs to verify byte-for-byte identical installs across prefixes ([#122](https://github.com/ocaml/ocamlfind/issues/122)).
- [@shym](https://github.com/shym) reviewed the PR commit-by-commit, offering detailed shell-scripting and OCaml-style suggestions on path handling, Makefile build rules, and the new CI workflow steps ([#122](https://github.com/ocaml/ocamlfind/issues/122)).

repositories.discussions_summary: Notable exchanges covered AI-assisted development disclosure, multi-line link escaping semantics, and cross-repository parameterized-library work.

repositories.emerging_trends:

repositories.discussions_summary: Reviewers debated package-removal policy after a checksum error and discussed naming and licensing for the new ocaml-sbom package.
repositories.notable_discussions:
- Reviewers debated whether to remove `simple_httpd.1.0` outright after a checksum error, favoring `available: false` per the repository's package-removal policy, with input from [Jan Midtgaard](https://github.com/jmid), [Hannes Mehnert](https://github.com/hannesm), [Marcello Seri](https://github.com/mseri) and [Dmitrii Kosarev](https://github.com/Kakadu) ([#30330](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/issues/30330), [#30123](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/issues/30123))

repositories.activity_summary: CI workflow dependency bumps opened by Dependabot, plus continued review of a Wasm runtime asset-resolution fix.
repositories.activity:
- Two **CI dependency bumps** were opened by [Dependabot](https://github.com/dependabot): `actions/setup-node` from 6 to 7 ([#2407](https://github.com/ocsigen/js_of_ocaml/pull/2407)), which remained open through the end of the week, and `tarides/changelog-check-action` from 3 to 4 ([#2408](https://github.com/ocsigen/js_of_ocaml/pull/2408)), which merged the same day, updating the `.github/workflows/changelog.yml` workflow.
- [Jérôme Vouillon](https://github.com/vouillon)'s **Wasm runtime asset-resolution fix** remained open under review, addressing a bug where the Node runtime located separately-compiled `.wasm` assets via `path.dirname(require.main.filename)` — the process entry point — causing lookups to fail when the program was loaded through `require` behind a CLI wrapper or a symlink, and to crash outright when `require.main` is undefined, such as in worker threads or `node -e`; the fix resolves assets relative to `module.filename` instead, matching the browser runtime's existing self-location via `document.currentScript.src`, with the same change applied to the WASI runtime ([#2389](https://github.com/ocsigen/js_of_ocaml/pull/2389)).

repositories.new_features_summary: Layout-polymorphic functions, unsigned unboxed integer primitive types, ocamldep `-modules-only`, and compact-frametable emitter plumbing.
repositories.new_features:
- **Layout-polymorphic functions** (`let poly_ f x = ...`) implemented across typedtree-to-tlambda and tlambda-to-slambda translation, along with application of such functions, by [Jack Rickard](https://github.com/Skepfyr) ([#5870](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/pull/5870))
- **Distinct unsigned unboxed integer primitive types** (`uint8_u`, `uint16_u`, `uint32_u`, `uint64_u`) added with the same kinds as their signed counterparts, letting the compiler distinguish signed and unsigned unboxed integers, by [Max Slater](https://github.com/TheNumbat) ([#6534](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/pull/6534)), which were then guarded behind the `small_numbers` extension along with a new `unativeint_u` type in the same follow-up ([#6634](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/pull/6634))
- New `-modules-only` flag for `ocamldep` that behaves like `-modules` but omits the leading `file:` prefix from each output line, letting build rules consume dependency output directly without shell postprocessing, by [Jakub Staroń](https://github.com/staronj) ([#6540](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/pull/6540))
- `-dprofile` now works in combination with `-stop-after middle_end`, fixing a case where profiling output was previously suppressed by the early exit, by [Basile Clément](https://github.com/bclement-ocp) ([#6550](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/pull/6550))
- Emitter plumbing added across backend code emitters to enable **compact frametables**, laying groundwork for shorter frametables tracked in [#6399](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6399), by [Nick Barnes](https://github.com/NickBarnes) ([#6488](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/pull/6488))
- New `split` statement added to `ocamltest`, by [Luke Maurer](https://github.com/lukemaurer) ([#6422](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/pull/6422))
- **Type shapes for `any` fields** implemented, allowing a type shape to be constructed even when field layouts of an `any`-kinded field are unknown, by [Luke Maurer](https://github.com/lukemaurer) ([#6403](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/pull/6403))
- Fixed a crash when an `any` type variable resolves to an unboxed product, by [Luke Maurer](https://github.com/lukemaurer) ([#6436](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/pull/6436))
- Fixed unsound argument value kinds in partial GADT matches, where calling-convention specialization could select the wrong value representation across GADT cases, by [Ryan Tjoa](https://github.com/rtjoa) ([#6356](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/pull/6356), [#6533](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/pull/6533))

repositories.brief_summary: Eio published the v1.4 release, adding `Flow.null` and a macOS select() fallback while improving error messages and pty handling.
repositories.new_features_summary: v1.4 shipped `Flow.null`, a macOS select() fallback for poll() failures, and improved error messages across networking and filesystem code.
repositories.new_features:
- Added `Flow.null`, a sink that discards all data until end-of-file and a source that immediately returns end-of-file, similar to `/dev/null`, by [Anil Madhavapeddy](https://github.com/avsm) and [Thomas Leonard](https://github.com/talex5), suggested by [Jon Sterling](https://github.com/jonsterling) ([#894](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/894))
- `eio_posix` now falls back to a custom `select()` stub for file descriptors where `poll()` fails with `POLLNVAL`, fixing a crash writing to `/dev/null` on macOS, by [Anil Madhavapeddy](https://github.com/avsm) ([#893](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/893), fixes [#757](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/757))
- `Net.getaddrinfo` and related lookup functions now include the queried hostname (and service) in raised error messages by [Thomas Leonard](https://github.com/talex5) ([#900](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/900))
- Fixed `eio_linux` directory reading so it no longer returns an empty batch before end-of-file, which could truncate listings on FUSE filesystems, by [Anil Madhavapeddy](https://github.com/avsm) ([#897](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/897))
- `eio_linux` now reports the real underlying error when `chmod` on a symlink fails via `/proc/self/fd/`, instead of masking it, by [Thomas Leonard](https://github.com/talex5) ([#901](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/901), test fix in [#903](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/903))
- `fork_action` now rejects uid/gid/pid values that don't fit the underlying C `uid_t`/`gid_t`/`pid_t` types instead of silently truncating them, by [Anil Madhavapeddy](https://github.com/avsm) ([#895](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/895))
- Function applications were eta-expanded to support compilation under **OxCaml** by [Anil Madhavapeddy](https://github.com/avsm) ([#898](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/898))
- `eio_unix_fork_error` now calls `_exit` automatically rather than relying on every caller to do so, by [Thomas Leonard](https://github.com/talex5) ([#896](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/896), fixes [#818](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/818))
- Published the **v1.4 release** with an updated `CHANGES.md` consolidating the above and prior work, by [Thomas Leonard](https://github.com/talex5) ([#904](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/904))
repositories.activity_summary: A pty EIO-to-EOF PR was opened while v1.4 shipped with error-message and platform fixes merged throughout the week.
repositories.activity:
- A PR converting tty `EIO` errors into `End_of_file` on Linux (and other platforms) for `Eio_unix.Pty` was opened by [Anil Madhavapeddy](https://github.com/avsm), addressing reads from a closed pty raising an unhandled I/O error ([#905](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/905), fixes [#902](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/902))
- The **v1.4 release** was published by [Thomas Leonard](https://github.com/talex5), bundling the `Flow.null` addition, macOS `select()` fallback, error-message improvements, and other fixes merged this week ([#904](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/904))
- Error reporting was tightened across the networking and filesystem stacks: `Net.getaddrinfo` failures now carry the queried hostname ([#900](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/900)), and `chmod` failures on symlinks report the real underlying error rather than a masked one ([#901](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/901), [#903](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/903))
- macOS-specific reliability work landed a custom `select()` stub used as a fallback when `poll()` returns `POLLNVAL` for device file descriptors such as `/dev/tty` or `/dev/null`, closing a longstanding crash reported by [Aaron Eline](https://github.com/aaronjeline) ([#893](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/893), [#757](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/757))
- `eio_linux` directory-entry reading and `fork_action` id handling were hardened by [Anil Madhavapeddy](https://github.com/avsm) ([#897](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/897), [#895](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/895)), alongside [Thomas Leonard](https://github.com/talex5)'s cleanup making `eio_unix_fork_error` call `_exit` automatically, closing a follow-up issue from [Patrick Ferris](https://github.com/patricoferris) ([#896](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/896), [#818](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/818))
- A `Flow.null` sink/source was added, motivated by a real-world use case from [Jon Sterling](https://github.com/jonsterling)'s Forester project, and evolved from an initial write-only sink to a combined source/sink during review by [Anil Madhavapeddy](https://github.com/avsm) and [Thomas Leonard](https://github.com/talex5) ([#894](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/894))
- Compatibility eta-expansion for **OxCaml** was merged by [Anil Madhavapeddy](https://github.com/avsm) ([#898](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/898))
- Two issues were reported by [Thomas Gazagnaire](https://github.com/samoht): a relative-path bug in `Eio.Path.mkdirs`, which was closed after investigation ([#906](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/906)), and a request to add a `~follow` argument to `open_in`/`open_out` for consistency with other path functions, which remains open ([#899](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/899))
repositories.discussions_summary: Discussions covered adding ~follow to open_in/open_out, pty EIO handling, and macOS select() implementation details.
repositories.notable_discussions:
- On [#899](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/899), [Thomas Gazagnaire](https://github.com/samoht) and [Thomas Leonard](https://github.com/talex5) discussed adding `~follow` to `open_in`/`open_out`, covering use cases like opening raw block devices with `O_NOFOLLOW` and safely building disk images from a source tree while guarding against symlink swaps mid-build
- On [#902](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/902), [Anil Madhavapeddy](https://github.com/avsm) and [Thomas Leonard](https://github.com/talex5) debated whether to wrap `Eio_unix.Pty` specifically or convert `EIO` to end-of-file generically whenever `isatty()` is true, settling on the general approach implemented in [#905](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/905)
- Review of the macOS `select()` fallback in [#893](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/893) covered platform-specific concerns including `fd_set` sizing beyond 1024 descriptors, whether to restrict the workaround to `__APPLE__` only, and correct `CAMLparam` usage in the new C stub
repositories.trends_summary: Error message quality and platform-specific edge-case hardening continued, culminating in the v1.4 release.
repositories.emerging_trends:
- Continued emphasis on **error message quality**, adding context such as hostnames and underlying errno values to exceptions rather than generic failures ([#900](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/900), [#901](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/901), [#903](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/903))
- Platform-edge-case hardening remains a recurring theme, spanning macOS `poll()`/`select()` behavior ([#893](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/893)), Linux `chmod` behavior on specific kernel/distro combinations ([#903](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/903)), and forward compatibility with the **OxCaml** compiler ([#898](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/898))
- The week closed with the **v1.4 release** ([#904](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/904)), consolidating several weeks of accumulated fixes and features into a single changelog

- Earlier `quickjs` 0.5.0 and `server-reason-react` 0.5.0 submissions by [David Sancho](https://github.com/davesnx) were superseded by 0.5.1 releases merged this week ([ocaml/opam-repository#30311](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/issues/30311), [ocaml/opam-repository#30312](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/issues/30312))
- On ocaml.org, [Nicolás Ojeda Bär](https://github.com/nojb) opened a **library team governance** documentation update ([ocaml/ocaml.org#3725](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml.org/issues/3725)); [Akhil Indurti](https://github.com/smasher164) opened a wasm-gc documentation fix for the WebAssembly tutorial ([ocaml/ocaml.org#3719](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml.org/issues/3719)); the opam package version display rework by [Sora Morimoto](https://github.com/smorimoto) continued under review awaiting [Jon Ludlam](https://github.com/jonludlam) ([ocaml/ocaml.org#3713](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml.org/issues/3713)); the automated platform-releases scrape PR remained open ([ocaml/ocaml.org#3693](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml.org/issues/3693)); and three automated Planet scrape runs merged new community blog and video content ([ocaml/ocaml.org#3720](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml.org/issues/3720), [ocaml/ocaml.org#3721](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml.org/issues/3721), [ocaml/ocaml.org#3724](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml.org/issues/3724))
group_summaries.cross_repository_work:

- [Jérôme Vouillon](https://github.com/vouillon) was active in both repositories: adding the new `theo` and `wax`/`wax-lib` opam packages ([ocaml/opam-repository#30279](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/issues/30279), [ocaml/opam-repository#30278](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/issues/30278)) while also syncing his personal blog into ocaml.org's Planet aggregator ([ocaml/ocaml.org#3722](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml.org/issues/3722))
- [Thomas Gazagnaire](https://github.com/samoht)'s new opam-repository packages `cascade` and `tw` ([ocaml/opam-repository#30280](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/issues/30280), [ocaml/opam-repository#30314](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/issues/30314)) coincided with his own Cascade and buffer-reuse articles being syndicated into ocaml.org's Planet feed via automated scraping ([ocaml/ocaml.org#3721](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml.org/issues/3721), [ocaml/ocaml.org#3724](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml.org/issues/3724))
- ocaml.org's opam package version display rework ([ocaml/ocaml.org#3713](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml.org/issues/3713)) directly concerns how opam-repository's own package release and version data is presented to end users
group_summaries.notable_discussions:
- opam-repository reviewers debated whether to remove `simple_httpd.1.0` outright after a checksum error, favoring `available: false` per repository policy, with input from [Jan Midtgaard](https://github.com/jmid), [Hannes Mehnert](https://github.com/hannesm), [Marcello Seri](https://github.com/mseri) and [Dmitrii Kosarev](https://github.com/Kakadu) ([ocaml/opam-repository#30330](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/issues/30330), [ocaml/opam-repository#30123](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/issues/30123))
- Naming and licensing of the new `ocaml-sbom` package were discussed against the policy discouraging `ocaml`-prefixed names, with [Jan Midtgaard](https://github.com/jmid) and [Raphaël Proust](https://github.com/raphael-proust) weighing an exception ([ocaml/opam-repository#30292](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/issues/30292))
- [Christophe Raffalli](https://github.com/craff) detailed platform-specific gaps in `conf-gles2`/`conf-gles3` coverage across openSUSE, FreeBSD and macOS, with a companion fix proposed ([ocaml/opam-repository#30336](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/issues/30336), [ocaml/opam-repository#30334](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/issues/30334))
- [Dmitri Volkov](https://github.com/sporkl) raised whether `conf-sdl2` should depend on `sdl2-compat` rather than `sdl2` on macOS, since Homebrew aliases the two ([ocaml/opam-repository#30337](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/issues/30337))
- A forum report that the opam package versions page could be misread as listing release dates and recommending every version shown, when dates actually reflect opam-repository submission times, led [Sora Morimoto](https://github.com/smorimoto) to rework the page's version selection and labeling ([ocaml/ocaml.org#3713](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml.org/issues/3713))
group_summaries.emerging_trends:
- **OCaml 5.5 readiness** work continues across opam-repository, including the macOS compiler-cloning fix ([ocaml/opam-repository#30317](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/issues/30317)) and the `ocamlfind` 5.5-compatible preview package ([ocaml/opam-repository#30285](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/issues/30285))
- Maintainers [Jan Midtgaard](https://github.com/jmid) and [Raphaël Proust](https://github.com/raphael-proust) are actively **triaging revdeps CI failures** before merging, catching regressions in `soteria` ([ocaml/opam-repository#30315](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/issues/30315)), `server-reason-react` ([ocaml/opam-repository#30311](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/issues/30311)) and `menhirformat` ([ocaml/opam-repository#30327](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/issues/30327))
- opam-repository's package-lifecycle policy favors `available: false` over deletion for broken submissions, and duplicate re-submitted PRs are closed rather than left open ([ocaml/opam-repository#30330](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/issues/30330), [ocaml/opam-repository#30331](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/issues/30331), [ocaml/opam-repository#30333](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/issues/30333))
- Contributors continue to submit **grouped multi-package releases** in single PRs, such as dune's 18 packages ([ocaml/opam-repository#30298](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/issues/30298)), eio's 5 packages ([ocaml/opam-repository#30318](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/issues/30318)), and the `hegel`/`ppx_hegel_*` group ([ocaml/opam-repository#30302](https://github.com/ocaml/opam-repository/issues/30302))
- Growing attention to **accuracy of package/version metadata** shown to end users, seen in ocaml.org's version-page rework prompted by forum feedback ([ocaml/ocaml.org#3713](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml.org/issues/3713)) and its wasm-gc documentation fix ([ocaml/ocaml.org#3719](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml.org/issues/3719))
- ocaml.org continues weekly automation of content sync via the **Planet blog/video scraper** ([ocaml/ocaml.org#3720](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml.org/issues/3720), [ocaml/ocaml.org#3721](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml.org/issues/3721), [ocaml/ocaml.org#3724](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml.org/issues/3724)) and dune platform release announcements kept in sync with upstream ([ocaml/ocaml.org#3704](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml.org/issues/3704), [ocaml/ocaml.org#3723](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml.org/issues/3723))

group_summaries.brief_summary: Dune shipped 3.24.1 and opam released 2.6.0-alpha1, fixing a same-day signing-key mixup, while merlin and ocaml-lsp advanced protocol work.
group_summaries.new_features_summary: Dune 3.24.1 and fish completion, opam 2.6.0-alpha1, merlin's open-record destructuring, and ocaml-lsp trace notifications shipped this week.
group_summaries.new_features:
- **[ocaml/dune](https://github.com/ocaml/dune)** released **3.24.1** ([ocaml/dune#15539](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15539)) bundling several backports, and separately merged fish-shell completion by [Chizy](https://github.com/chizy7) ([ocaml/dune#15515](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15515)), `dune promote` pending-file tab completion by [Ali Caglayan](https://github.com/Alizter) ([ocaml/dune#15338](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15338)), and a move of artifact-substitution I/O onto the background thread pool by [Antonio Nuno Monteiro](https://github.com/anmonteiro) ([ocaml/dune#15559](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15559), [ocaml/dune#15598](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15598))
- **[ocaml/merlin](https://github.com/ocaml/merlin)** shipped destructuring of **open record patterns** by [Paul-Elliot Anglès d'Auriac](https://github.com/panglesd), resolving a request open since 2015 ([ocaml/merlin#2103](https://github.com/ocaml/merlin/issues/2103), fixes [ocaml/merlin#436](https://github.com/ocaml/merlin/issues/436)), and exposed a `parse_warnings` API by [PixieDust](https://github.com/PizieDust) ([ocaml/merlin#2088](https://github.com/ocaml/merlin/issues/2088))
- **[ocaml/opam](https://github.com/ocaml/opam)** released **2.6.0-alpha1** by [Kate](https://github.com/kit-ty-kate), bundling `.install` `root`/`rootexec` sections ([ocaml/opam#6938](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/6938)) and a new `--ignore-available-on` flag ([ocaml/opam#6836](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/6836))
- **[ocaml/ocaml-lsp](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp)** added LSP **trace notifications** for Dune RPC and build-progress activity ([ocaml/ocaml-lsp#1899](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/1899)), a code action to open the closest Dune file ([ocaml/ocaml-lsp#1817](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/1817)), and operator-aware semantic highlighting ([ocaml/ocaml-lsp#1831](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/1831)), all by [Rudi Grinberg](https://github.com/rgrinberg)
group_summaries.group_overview:

- **[ocaml/ocamlfind](https://github.com/ocaml/ocamlfind)**: no merges this week; detailed commit-by-commit review continued on [David Allsopp](https://github.com/dra27)'s relocatable-install PR ([ocaml/ocamlfind#122](https://github.com/ocaml/ocamlfind/issues/122))
- **[ocaml/odoc](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc)**: three OxCaml-compatibility PRs opened by [@art-w](https://github.com/art-w) ([ocaml/odoc#1464](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/issues/1464), [ocaml/odoc#1466](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/issues/1466), [ocaml/odoc#1467](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/issues/1467)); only a CI-action bump merged ([ocaml/odoc#1463](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/issues/1463))

- **ocaml-dune/spawn**: no recorded activity this week

- **[ocsigen/js_of_ocaml](https://github.com/ocsigen/js_of_ocaml)**: [Jérôme Vouillon](https://github.com/vouillon)'s Wasm/WASI asset-resolution fix remained under review ([ocsigen/js_of_ocaml#2389](https://github.com/ocsigen/js_of_ocaml/pull/2389)); Dependabot merged a changelog-action bump ([ocsigen/js_of_ocaml#2408](https://github.com/ocsigen/js_of_ocaml/pull/2408))
group_summaries.activity_summary: Ocaml-lsp closed a large OCaml test-suite rewrite while dune and merlin opened new tooling PRs and triaged Windows and staleness bugs.
group_summaries.activity:
- **[ocaml/dune](https://github.com/ocaml/dune)**: new unmerged PRs cover anonymous-action/alias semantics ([ocaml/dune#15581](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15581)), a `dune describe --include-empty` flag ([ocaml/dune#15585](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15585)), and a `dune shell` debugging prototype by [Ali Caglayan](https://github.com/Alizter) ([ocaml/dune#15597](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15597)); [Kris De Volder](https://github.com/kdvolder)'s report of a silent `dune exec` hang on `execve` failure ([ocaml/dune#15602](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15602)) was covered with regression tests the same day by [Antonio Nuno Monteiro](https://github.com/anmonteiro) ([ocaml/dune#15603](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15603))
- **[ocaml/merlin](https://github.com/ocaml/merlin)**: six PRs opened remain unmerged, including a typing-recovery preview by [Xavier Van de Woestyne](https://github.com/xvw) ([ocaml/merlin#2087](https://github.com/ocaml/merlin/issues/2087)) and a regression test reproducing stale load paths by [Rudi Grinberg](https://github.com/rgrinberg) ([ocaml/merlin#2109](https://github.com/ocaml/merlin/issues/2109)); seven long-dormant issues from 2015-2021 were closed after backlog review led by [Ulysse](https://github.com/voodoos)
- **[ocaml/opam](https://github.com/ocaml/opam)**: [Brian Ward](https://github.com/WardBrian)'s multi-PR cmdliner-based completion rewrite continued across four dependent PRs ([ocaml/opam#6812](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/pull/6812), [ocaml/opam#6867](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/pull/6867), [ocaml/opam#6868](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/pull/6868), [ocaml/opam#6869](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/pull/6869)), and [yannl35133](https://github.com/yannl35133) opened a clearer `opam repo add` error message ([ocaml/opam#7014](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/pull/7014))
- **[ocaml/ocaml-lsp](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp)**: the **OCaml-native test-suite rewrite** ([ocaml/ocaml-lsp#1063](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/1063)) closed this week after converting dozens of bug reproductions into property-based tests; twenty further PRs opened on diagnostics pulls, code-action resolution, and semantic-token classification, and a batch of a dozen-plus long-standing issues were triaged and closed
- **[ocaml/odoc](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc)**: review continued on [Tim ats](https://github.com/Tim-ats-d)'s multi-line link-parsing fix, with detailed feedback from [Paul-Elliot Anglès d'Auriac](https://github.com/panglesd) on escaping semantics ([ocaml/odoc#1439](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/issues/1439))
group_summaries.cross_repository_work:
- **odoc ↔ dune**: [Shon Feder](https://github.com/shonfeder)'s odoc issue requesting parameterized-library rendering ([ocaml/odoc#1390](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/issues/1390)) references dune's own parameterized-library evaluation work ([ocaml/dune#12565](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/12565)); [@art-w](https://github.com/art-w) opened the odoc-side implementation this week ([ocaml/odoc#1464](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/issues/1464))
- **merlin ↔ ocaml-lsp**: [PixieDust](https://github.com/PizieDust) exposed a `parse_warnings` API in merlin ([ocaml/merlin#2088](https://github.com/ocaml/merlin/issues/2088)) as a prerequisite for their companion ocaml-lsp PR to surface hover information on warnings ([ocaml/ocaml-lsp#1606](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/1606)), addressing a request open since 2022 ([ocaml/ocaml-lsp#717](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/717))
- **merlin ↔ ocaml-lsp**: [Rudi Grinberg](https://github.com/rgrinberg) opened a merlin regression test for stale load paths across typer states ([ocaml/merlin#2109](https://github.com/ocaml/merlin/issues/2109)) the same week he fixed the related recurring "Unbound module" diagnostic in ocaml-lsp by resetting Merlin load paths after Dune builds ([ocaml/ocaml-lsp#1872](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/1872), closing [ocaml/ocaml-lsp#1209](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/1209))
- **dune ↔ js_of_ocaml**: dune fixed `build_runtime_flags` being silently ignored for `js_of_ocaml`/`wasm_of_ocaml` executables in separate compilation mode ([ocaml/dune#15455](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15455)), and its 3.24.1 release credits [Jérôme Vouillon](https://github.com/vouillon) for an earlier js_of_ocaml-related archive-rule fix
- **merlin → ocaml/ocaml (compiler)**: [Xavier Van de Woestyne](https://github.com/xvw) opened an upstream compiler PR to bring Typedtree continuation-info patches into the OCaml compiler itself, part of merlin's compiler-upstreamings tracking issue ([ocaml/ocaml#14946](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14946), tracked via [ocaml/merlin#2091](https://github.com/ocaml/merlin/issues/2091))
group_summaries.notable_discussions:
- On the dune 3.24.1 release tracker, [Ali Caglayan](https://github.com/Alizter) posted a detailed opam-CI triage summary covering 18 packages across 1,314 variants with no Dune-attributable regressions, and explained that a DragonFlyBSD support fix would wait for 3.25 rather than the patch release ([ocaml/dune#15439](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15439))
- [Rudi Grinberg](https://github.com/rgrinberg) and [Nat Karmios](https://github.com/NatKarmios) debated why anonymous dune actions attached to multiple aliases produce surprising inter-alias dependencies, agreeing human-readable action IDs were worth adding for `dune shell` ([ocaml/dune#15576](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15576))
- [Akhil](https://github.com/akhiltulluri) reported merlin-lib failing to build against **OCaml 5.5.0**; [Ulysse](https://github.com/voodoos) and [Kate](https://github.com/kit-ty-kate) discussed possible stale-stdlib causes without reproducing it on macOS ([ocaml/merlin#2108](https://github.com/ocaml/merlin/issues/2108))
- [@shym](https://github.com/shym) suggested in review that relocatable installation should become Findlib's default behaviour rather than an opt-in mode ([ocaml/ocamlfind#122](https://github.com/ocaml/ocamlfind/issues/122))
- [Benjamin Canou](https://github.com/klakplok) disclosed that his odoc fix was developed with AI assistance, with the regression test written by Claude ([ocaml/odoc#1465](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/issues/1465))
- The **opam 2.6.0-alpha1 release signature** was found to use the wrong GPG subkey shortly after publishing; [Andriy Sultanov](https://github.com/last-genius) reported the failure and [Kate](https://github.com/kit-ty-kate) traced it to a key-transfer mistake and re-signed the release the same day ([ocaml/opam#7049](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/7049))
- [Sora Morimoto](https://github.com/smorimoto) documented a git fsmonitor socket breaking `opam repository set-url` and repository updates ([ocaml/opam#7054](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/7054))
group_summaries.emerging_trends:
- **AI-assisted contributions** recurred across repos: a Windows fix authored directly by the `copilot-swe-agent` bot in merlin ([ocaml/merlin#2095](https://github.com/ocaml/merlin/issues/2095)), [Carine Morel](https://github.com/lyrm) disclosing Claude-assisted diagnosis before hand-authoring a merlin fix ([ocaml/merlin#2089](https://github.com/ocaml/merlin/issues/2089)), and a Claude-written regression test in odoc ([ocaml/odoc#1465](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/issues/1465))
- **Relocatable, reproducible installs** are a shared theme ahead of OCaml 5.5: ocamlfind's in-progress relocatable-install PR ([ocaml/ocamlfind#122](https://github.com/ocaml/ocamlfind/issues/122)) follows the definition proposed in [ocaml/RFCs#53](https://github.com/ocaml/RFCs/issues/53), while opam 2.6.0-alpha1 shipped `root`/`rootexec` `.install` sections for prefix-relative installs ([ocaml/opam#6938](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/6938))
- **Parallel shell-completion rewrites**: dune shipped fish-shell completion and opened an issue to upstream it into `cmdliner` itself ([ocaml/dune#15583](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/15583)), while opam's independent cmdliner-based completion overhaul continued across four PRs ([ocaml/opam#6812](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/pull/6812), [ocaml/opam#6867](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/pull/6867), [ocaml/opam#6868](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/pull/6868), [ocaml/opam#6869](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/pull/6869))
- **Backlog grooming** of long-dormant issues stood out in both merlin (seven issues from 2015-2021 closed, [ocaml/merlin#436](https://github.com/ocaml/merlin/issues/436), [ocaml/merlin#1384](https://github.com/ocaml/merlin/issues/1384)) and ocaml-lsp (a dozen-plus old reports closed alongside the [ocaml/ocaml-lsp#1063](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/1063) test-suite rewrite)
- **OxCaml compiler compatibility** continued incrementally in odoc, with three of four PRs opened this week addressing kind abbreviations, with-bounds handling, and parameterized libraries ([ocaml/odoc#1467](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/issues/1467), [ocaml/odoc#1466](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/issues/1466), [ocaml/odoc#1464](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/issues/1464))
- **Concentrated solo maintenance** in ocaml-lsp, where nearly all merged and opened work this week came from [Rudi Grinberg](https://github.com/rgrinberg)
